findings.title: Coupon banner close control has a 16x16 px hit target
findings.state: Cart page with coupon banner visible, default state
steps: Read measured geometry of #promo-close from the snapshot
findings.expected: A mobile close control has a touch target of at least 24x24 px (commonly 44x44 px); the same control on the case-2 sample measures 44x44.
findings.observed: The #promo-close button's measured box is 16x16 CSS px at (318, 86); the neighboring 받기 button is 56x44. A tap at the center (326, 94) hit the target, but the tappable area is far smaller than the control next to it and than the equivalent control in case-2.

findings.title: Destructive 전체삭제 button sits flush beside the primary pay button in the sticky footer
steps: Observe cart page after closing the banner (S-case-1-002)
Compare footer geometry: #btn-clear at x=16..100 y=716 (84x52), #pay at x=104..344 y=716 (240x52)
findings.expected: A destructive clear-cart action is separated from the primary payment CTA, as in case-2 where 전체 삭제 is a text button at the top of the list and the footer contains only the pay button.
findings.observed: A red-bordered destructive button (roles: destructive, border #d32f2f) sits in the same sticky bottom bar, 4 px to the left of the primary pay button, so a slightly leftward mis-tap deletes all cart items instead of paying.

limitations: Only the happy path (close banner, select 토스페이, pay) was exercised.
No near-miss tap testing for the 16x16 close target; no test of paying without selecting a payment method.
No findings on the exercised path; only the happy path (close banner, confirm 토스페이 default, pay) was tested.
Empty cart, payment failure, and the '다른 결제 수단 9개 보기' expander were not exercised.

findings.title: Validation error is not tied to the offending phone field (no invalid state, no association, focus stays on submit)
findings.state: After submitting the booking form with the phone number empty
steps: Fill name 테스트, check consent, submit with phone empty
Read the error alert and inspect #phone
findings.expected: The invalid field is programmatically marked and associated with its message (e.g., aria-invalid + aria-describedby), so both visual and assistive-technology users can locate it; case-4 does this.
findings.observed: A role=alert box appears at the top of the form ('입력 내용을 확인해 주세요. / 휴대폰 번호를 정확히 입력해 주세요.'), but #phone reports invalid:false, aria_invalid:null, described_by:[], error_associated:false, keeps its normal border (#8b95a1), and focus remains on #submit. Nothing on the field itself shows the error.

findings.title: Error alert stays visible after the value is corrected; it clears only on resubmission
findings.state: After typing the corrected phone number 010-0000-0000
steps: Submit with phone empty so the alert shows
findings.expected: Error feedback clears or updates when the field content changes.
findings.observed: The full alert text remains visible with the corrected value already entered; only the next submit removes it.

limitations: Only the intended flow (miss phone, follow guidance, resubmit) was exercised; one date/time combination was used.
Keyboard-only navigation and near-miss taps were not tested.

findings.title: Inline error and footer alert persist after the value is corrected; they clear only on resubmission
findings.state: After typing the corrected phone number 010-0000-0000
steps: Submit with phone empty (inline error + footer alert appear, field marked aria-invalid=true)
findings.expected: Error feedback clears or updates when the field content changes.
findings.observed: Both the inline '⚠ 휴대폰 번호를 정확히 입력해 주세요. 예: 010-1234-5678' and the footer '⚠ 휴대폰 번호를 확인해 주세요.' remain visible with the corrected value entered; only the next submit clears them.

findings.title: Focus stays on the submit button after the validation failure
findings.state: Immediately after the failed submit with empty phone
steps: Read focus state via the provided inspect interface
findings.expected: Focus moves to the first invalid field (or its error is otherwise directly reachable) so keyboard users can correct it without searching.
findings.observed: Focus remains on #submit; #phone is marked aria-invalid=true with the inline message, but the user must move focus back up to the field manually.

limitations: Only the intended flow (miss phone, follow guidance, resubmit) was exercised; one date/time combination was used.
Near-miss taps and keyboard-only traversal were not tested.

overall_limitations: All pages are offline synthetic samples; results cover only the four assigned tasks on build bda38f67f8ff4b5f56588d487430c282d1483be1 (galaxy-s24 viewport 360x780).
State observations come from the provided observe/inspect interface and the driver's screenshots; no page source or JS was read.

The first case-3 server launch failed inside the sandbox (Chromium launch blocked); it was rerun with escalated permissions as the brief allows. The failed run directory is preserved as runs/case-3-launchfailed and is not part of the results.
Each case ran as its own server session on port 9604 with fresh state; no findings depend on cross-case state.
